title: CoherentFormalModulesFiniteProducts
statement: Let $X$ be a Noetherian scheme and $\mathcal I\subseteq\mathcal O_X$ a quasi-coherent ideal sheaf. The property of being a coherent adic inverse system [def-weil-pbc-coherent-formal-module] is closed under finite products in the ambient category of inverse systems of $\mathcal O_X$-modules. Explicitly, the limit of every finite discrete diagram of systems satisfying that property also satisfies it, including the empty product.

source.place: Cohomology of Schemes, Lemma 087X (lemma-inverse-systems-abelian), additive structure (written out from Section 087V)

proof.text: For the empty product, use the zero inverse system. Its terms are coherent and its ideal products and quotients are zero. For a binary product use the termwise biproduct. Its terms are coherent by [lem-weil-pbc-coherent-kernel-cokernel-locnoeth]. On every affine open the section description in [lem-weil-pbc-ideal-times-quasi-coherent-affine-sections] identifies the ideal product with $I^n(P\oplus Q)=I^nP\oplus I^nQ$. Thus annihilation and reduction commute with the biproduct. The specified quotient isomorphisms of the two factors give the quotient isomorphism of their sum, with the required transition equality.

Induct over the cardinality of a finite discrete diagram, using zero and binary products. Any other limiting cone is uniquely isomorphic to this one. Component isomorphisms transport coherence, ideal annihilation and the specified reduction isomorphisms, so its vertex also satisfies the object property.
